findings.summary: isPublished(article) is called as isPublished(articles.get(match[1])) (line 44) for every /blog/<slug> link. If the slug doesn't match any file in the articles directory (typo, renamed/removed post), .get() returns undefined and isPublished immediately does `article.draft`, throwing. Reproduced live: appending a link to a nonexistent slug in an existing published article and running `pnpm -F @jasonmatthew/web build` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'draft')` from @mdx-js/rollup and fails the whole site build. No current content triggers this (verified via grep of all /blog/ links), but the very next mistyped internal link will take down the build with an opaque error, which is a worse outcome than the dead/premature link this feature exists to prevent.

findings.summary: The implementer's report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff contains no test files, and the repo has no test infrastructure at all (no vitest, no *.test.* files anywhere, no test script in package.json). This claim is false as stated. Verification of the feature was instead done by inspecting build output, which is fine as a manual check but is not what the report claims.

findings.summary: This file's isPublished() duplicates apps/web/src/utils/data-utils.ts's isPublished but omits its `import.meta.env.DEV` bypass. Elsewhere on the site, DEV mode shows scheduled/future-dated posts in listings so authors can preview them locally; this plugin doesn't get that bypass, so during `pnpm dev` a link between two upcoming posts still gets silently downgraded to plain text even though both posts are visible in the dev preview. Minor because it only affects local preview fidelity, not production, and brief's own stated rule ("not draft and not future-dated") doesn't mention a DEV carve-out.

findings.summary: loadArticles() re-reads and re-parses every file in the articles directory from scratch on every single transform invocation, i.e. once per markdown/MDX file processed anywhere on the site (articles, projects, and pages all run through it, since it's registered globally in markdown.remarkPlugins rather than scoped to the blog collection). At current scale (~16 articles, 48 pages, ~2s total build) this is invisible, but it's O(total content files x article files) redundant disk reads for no benefit over computing the index once per build.
